\(\sqrt{2}\,x^2 + 7x + 5\sqrt{2} = 0\) to solve this quadratic equation by factorisation, complete the following activity.

Solution : \(\sqrt{2}\,x^2 + 7x + 5\sqrt{2} = 0\)

\(\sqrt{2}\,x^2 + \square + \square + 5\sqrt{2} = 0\)

\(x(\ldots\ldots) + \sqrt{2}(\ldots\ldots) = 0\)

\((\ldots\ldots)(x + \sqrt{2}) = 0\)

\((\ldots\ldots) = 0\) or \((x + \sqrt{2}) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = \square\) or \(x = -\sqrt{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\square\) and \(-\sqrt{2}\) are roots of the equation.
note: Printed as a fill-in-the-boxes activity but numbered as a sub-item of exercise Q.1, so it is ingested; the boxes are reproduced as printed.
